rows.label: Where do errors come from?
rows.symptom: Errors are often a result of worker carelessness.
rows.rootCause: Errors are the result of defects in the system. People are only part of the process.

rows.label: How should we respond?
rows.symptom: We need to train and motivate workers to be more careful.
rows.rootCause: We need to find out why this is happening, and implement mistake-proofs so it won't happen again.

rows.label: Is it worth fixing?
rows.symptom: We don't have the time or resources to really get to the bottom of this problem.
rows.rootCause: This is critical. We need to fix it for good, or it will come back and burn us.

symbols.name: Data Box

persuasion.title: Psychology of persuasion
persuasion.principlesTitle: Robert Cialdini’s Six Principles of Influence

principles.name: Reciprocity
principles.definition: When we receive something, we feel obliged to give something back.

principles.name: Consistency
principles.definition: We feel compelled to be consistent with what we’ve said/done in the past.

principles.name: Social Proof
principles.definition: When we’re uncertain how to behave or react, we look to others for answers.

principles.name: Liking
principles.definition: We’re more likely to agree to someone’s request if we know and like him/her.

principles.name: Authority
principles.definition: We tend to obey figures of authority (people with titles or expertise).

principles.name: Scarcity
principles.definition: We perceive something to be more valuable when it’s less available.
